mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the periods following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 0.5%, it indicates a monetary easing that can stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 55% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both GDP and housing starts indicates strong demand, which can drive corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in industrial production during a late-cycle expansion may lead to supply chain constraints, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Real consumer spending growth indicates strong demand, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over a short horizon of 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 45% of the periods following RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 50% of the periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with high unemployment indicates a specific policy stance that may lead to market uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is low and UNRATE is high, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth during an economic expansion indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.
